title: Large step size makes gradient descent on x^2 converge faster
question: Does increasing the learning rate always speed up convergence on a quadratic?
hypothesis: Plain gradient descent on f(x)=x^2 with learning rate 2.5 reaches |x| < 1e-3 within 50 steps from x0=1.
setup: examples/repro/gd_quadratic.py; x0 = 1, 50 steps, update x <- x - lr * 2x.
outcome: |x| grows by a factor of 4 per step and ends near 1.3e30.
scope: Only f(x)=x^2 with plain gradient descent and lr = 2.5. Says nothing about lr <= 1 or about other objectives.
cause: The update multiplies x by (1 - 2*lr) = -4; any lr > 1 makes |1 - 2*lr| > 1, so iterates diverge.
follow_up: Format example only. Real records live in ledger/.
